question: to the Commission Alex Agius Saliba (S&D) Subject:

Following the Council decision of 12 December 2025 to remove the customs duty de minimis threshold, the temporary framework expected to apply from 1 July 2026 raises important questions regarding its operational implementation across the Union. In particular, concerns arise as to whether proposed changes affecting the simplified electronic customs declaration (H7 declaration), additional data requirements and the rules on direct and indirect representation may introduce disproportionate administrative complexity and require substantial systems adjustments for operators handling high volumes of low-value consignments. Such changes may risk affecting the efficiency, consistency and timely processing of crossborder postal traffic, with possible implications for consumers and the functioning of the internal market. In light of the above, can the Commission clarify the following: 1.
How will it ensure that the proposed customs data requirements remain compatible with Universal Postal Union standards and globally harmonised postal data formats?
Has it assessed the risk that diverging data requirements may disrupt international postal exchanges?
Will it coordinate with international postal bodies before finalising any additional obligations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.6.2026) The Council adopted the elimination of the EUR 150 customs duty exemption in January 2026. The Commission and the Member States must ensure that the temporary EUR 3 customs duty is effectively collected from 1 July 2026, including in postal flow. The new rules will make e-commerce platforms and sellers primarily responsible for payment and make use of the existing customs legislation and IT systems. The Commission recognises the Universal Postal Union (UPU) legal framework and acknowledges the challenges expressed by EU postal operators. EU secondary legislation lays down common rules and definitions to avoid diverging data requirements across the EU and to ensure that all flows are treated similarly, without creating loopholes. The Commission published a guidance document for customs authorities and stakeholders on 3 June 20261. This guidance highlights specific options for postal operators. During the legislative process, the Commission has consulted postal operators operating under the UPU legal framework and will continue this dialogue. The Commission will closely monitor the implementation of the temporary EUR 3 customs duty and address relevant issues in the review of Council Regulation (EU) 2026/3822.
